title: Days Between Dates and Weekday
statement: You get two dates, A and B, in YYYY-MM-DD form. Print the number of days you must move from A to reach B. The number is negative if B is before A. Then print the day of the week of A in capital English letters, such as MONDAY. Remember that leap years add one day to February.
inputFormat: Two lines. Line 1 has date A. Line 2 has date B. Both are real calendar dates written with leading zeros.
outputFormat: One line: the signed number of days from A to B, a space, then the weekday of A in capital letters.
constraints: Both dates exist in the calendar
Use the normal Gregorian leap year rule (2100 is not a leap year)
explanations: 2024 is a leap year. January has 31 days and February has 29, so March 1 is 60 days later. January 1, 2024 was a Monday.
B is 5 days before A, so the answer is negative. August 15, 2023 was a Tuesday.
reference:
import sys, datetime
a, b = sys.stdin.read().split()
def p(s):
    y, m, d = map(int, s.split('-'))
    return datetime.date(y, m, d)
x = p(a)
y = p(b)
names = ["MONDAY", "TUESDAY", "WEDNESDAY", "THURSDAY", "FRIDAY", "SATURDAY", "SUNDAY"]
print((y - x).days, names[x.weekday()])
